title: Monitoring Export v1 — qualifier vocabulary
description:
Shared definitions for every value the LLS Monitoring Backend exports to algomatric.in.

The central rule: a monitored value is never a bare scalar. It is a QualifiedValue carrying an explicit knowledge state, so that absence of knowledge survives transport and reaches the screen as absence of knowledge. The dashboard is forbidden from collapsing UNKNOWN into 0 / false / healthy / flat, and this schema makes that collapse impossible to express on the wire.

Timestamp.description: RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 with an explicit offset. UTC (trailing Z) is preferred. A timestamp without an offset is a schema violation, not something to guess at.

KnowledgeState.description:
What the Monitoring Backend actually knows about this value.

KNOWN            — observed, current, trusted. The only state that means 'this is the value'.
UNKNOWN          — the source cannot say. No value is carried. Never render as zero/empty/healthy.
STALE            — a value was known, but it is past its validity point. Carries the value AND as_of.
UNTRUSTED        — a value exists but the source does not vouch for it (degraded input, failed check).
INCOMPLETE       — a partial answer: some contributing inputs are missing. May carry a partial value.
UNSUPPORTED      — this source/build cannot produce this field at all. Structurally absent, not missing.
NOT_APPLICABLE   — the field has no meaning in this context (e.g. fill price on an unfilled order).
SIMULATED        — produced by simulation/replay, not live observation. Carries a value; never 'live'.
SYNTHETIC_CLOCK  — produced under an artificial clock. Carries a value; timings are not wall-clock.

QualifiedValue.description: Base shape for every exported value. Specialisations below constrain the type of `value`; the presence rules are identical for all of them.

value.description: The value itself. Present only for states that carry one (see the allOf rules). Its absence is meaningful and must not be filled in downstream.

as_of.description: The instant this value was last true. Required when state is STALE; useful on any state.

reason.description: Why the state is not KNOWN, in the source's own words. Displayed verbatim; never parsed for meaning by the dashboard.

source_state.description: The raw state token used inside LLS, preserved unmapped. Lets a forensic view show what the source actually said even after normalisation.

QualifiedRatio.description: A fraction in [0,1] supplied by the source. The dashboard must never compute one of these from counts it happens to hold.

QualifiedDurationMs.description: A duration in milliseconds, already computed by the Monitoring Backend from timestamps it knows to be clock-compatible.

ClockDomain.description: Which clock a timestamp was read from. Two timestamps may only be subtracted when they share a domain and both carry acceptable quality — the Monitoring Backend enforces this and exports the resulting interval, not the operands.

ClockQuality.description:
How much the source trusts the clock behind a timestamp.

DISCIPLINED   — synchronised, bounded error.
DEGRADED      — synchronisation suspect; intervals are indicative only.
UNDISCIPLINED — free-running; do not derive intervals.
SYNTHETIC     — artificial time (replay/simulation).
UNKNOWN       — the source cannot characterise it.

Clock.description: Clock characterisation attached to a timestamp or an interval calculation.

offset_ms.description: Source's estimate of this clock's offset from reference, if it has one.

Freshness.description: The source's own statement of how long this observation stays valid. The dashboard compares its display time against `stale_after` — it does not invent a staleness policy of its own, and it does not decide something is still fresh because it looks recent.

data_as_of.description: The instant the payload describes. Distinct from when the message was generated.

stale_after.description: After this instant the dashboard MUST present the payload as STALE, whether or not newer data has arrived. Omitted only when the source genuinely has no validity horizon.

state.description: The source's assessment at generation time. `stale_after` governs afterwards.

expected_interval_ms.description: How often this observation is expected to be republished. Lets the dashboard show 'overdue' without guessing a cadence.

TrustLevel.description:
How the Monitoring Backend came to believe this, strongest first.

AUTHORITATIVE — from the system of record for this fact.
CORROBORATED  — independently agreed by two or more sources.
REPORTED      — single-source assertion, unverified.
INFERRED      — derived by correlation/reconstruction, not directly observed.
UNTRUSTED     — retained as evidence, explicitly not to be relied on.
UNKNOWN       — the backend cannot characterise its own confidence.

basis.description: Why this level. Free text, shown verbatim in forensic views.

confidence.description: Numeric confidence, only when the backend genuinely produces one.

Coverage.description: How much of what should have been observed actually was. Every number here is supplied by the Monitoring Backend. The dashboard renders UNKNOWN rather than dividing `observed` by `expected` itself — a coverage figure the source did not assert is a fabricated figure.

basis.description: What population the ratio is over, in the source's words.

SourceAuthority.description: Whose version of reality a fact represents. Positions and fills in particular must stay attributable — a Core-asserted position and a broker-reported position are different claims and are displayed as such, never merged into one number.

Derivation.description: How this observation came to exist.

EvidenceRef.description: An opaque pointer into Black Box evidence. algomatric.in stores and displays these; it never dereferences them into LLS, and never alters them.

kind.description: Evidence class, e.g. 'capture', 'log_segment', 'frame'. Opaque to the dashboard.

ref.description: Opaque identifier within the Black Box.

digest.description: Content digest, when the source computes one.

Provenance.description: Where this observation came from and what produced it.

capture_id.description: Black Box capture this observation belongs to, where the concept applies.

Qualifiers.description: The qualifier block carried by every observation payload. Together these answer the six questions a live panel must be able to answer: when was this generated, when received, what is it valid as of, is it stale, is the source healthy, is the data complete.
